messages.text: St Leger: Big race runners guide

metadata.summary: As the United States Of America celebrates its 250th anniversary, so does the world’s oldest Classic race. How many sporting events last this long? Very few.
metadata.content: St Leger: Mike Cattermole's big race runners guide | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content St Leger: Mike Cattermole's big race runners guide With the 250th instalment of the world's oldest Classic on the horizon, Sky Sports Racing's Mike Cattermole runs through every contender going to post on Town Moor at 3.35pm on Saturday; Watch the race live from Doncaster on Sky Sports Racing. Thursday 10 September 2026 12:18, UK Image: Scandinavia won the 2025 renewal of the St Leger As the United States Of America celebrates its 250th anniversary, so does the world’s oldest Classic race. How many sporting events last this long? Very few. So, who will take Saturday's special renewal of the Betfred St Leger? First of all, it's great to see the Derby winner, Christmas Day, lining up. Not all that many do the double, a fact that I appreciated early in my racing life when even the mighty Shergar could manage only fourth. In more recent years, Camelot just missed out on his Triple Crown attempt. Remember, the Leger is only a furlong and a half shorter than two miles but you still need speed as well as stamina to take it. Never Say Die, St Paddy, Nijinksy and Reference Point are the last four to have backed up here after Epsom, however, so good luck to Christmas Day. Leger tips! messages.text: Humphries: Opening up on mental health was best choice I ever made

metadata.summary: World No 2 Luke Humphries said his rise to the top of darts would never have been possible had he not opened up about his mental health struggles.
metadata.content: Luke Humphries says opening up about his mental health helped him rise to the top of darts | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to content Luke Humphries says opening up about his mental health helped him rise to the top of darts Luke Humphries has been hailed for opening up about his mental health issues; the world No 2 believes speaking about his struggles has helped him rise to the top of darts Thursday 10 September 2026 12:33, UK Image: Luke Humphries says opening up about his mental health struggles helped him rise to the top of darts World No 2 Luke Humphries said his rise to the top of darts would never have been possible had he not opened up about his mental health struggles. Humphries, who has partnered with the Samaritans to mark World Suicide Prevention Day, was on the grind of the PDC Tour when he suffered an anxiety attack midway through a tournament in 2019 and considered quitting. He spoke openly about his troubles, and it had a positive impact on him as he surged to the top of the game, culminating in winning the 2024 World Championship title and becoming world No 1. "For me, the best thing I ever did was go and see a doctor and go and tell him my feelings," Humphries said in conversation with a Samaritans volunteer. Image: Humphries went on to win the 2024 PDC World Darts Championship title and became world No 1 "Look who I am now. I've achieved so much from doing that and I'm so glad I did. messages.text: Arteta explains new role for transformed Odegaard

metadata.summary: Martin Odegaard is a player transformed at the start of this season - and Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta puts his captain's impressive form down to fitness and new positioning.
metadata.content: Arsenal: Martin Odegaard new role explained by Mikel Arteta after captain's Champions League winner at Napoli | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Arsenal: Martin Odegaard new role explained by Mikel Arteta after captain's Champions League winner at Napoli Martin Odegaard scored his fourth goal in five games this season with the winner in Arsenal's 1-0 Champions League victory at Napoli on Wednesday; Gunners captain only scored once in 2025/26 but higher position and fitness have facilitated fast start to the new campaign By Peter Smith and Nick Wright Thursday 10 September 2026 08:54, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Cotterill is in Naples as Arsenal beat Napoli 1-0 in their opening match of the Champions League this season. Martin Odegaard is a player transformed at the start of this season - and Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta puts his captain's impressive form down to fitness and new positioning. Odegaard was the match-winner again for Arsenal on Wednesday, thumping in the only goal of the game in the Champions League victory at Napoli. That hit followed his clinching strike against Chelsea in the Premier League on Sunday and takes his total to four goals in five appearances this season across all competitions. Odegaard only scored once for Arsenal during an injury-hit 2025/26 campaign but now his stats are up across a range of other attacking metrics, too.
